title: Eddie Mallory's band at the Villa de Nice and its European acts
summary: After the Gold Coast folded Wilson joined Eddie Mallory at Buchet's, playing for Sally Rand's first club act, classical arias and European acts as well as dance music.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, did you work with Papa Bouchet's band at the Villa DeNice?

Yes, but that was later -- after the Gold Coast job folded, then I joined Eddie Mallory's band and that's where I worked with Budd Johnson and Keg Johnson. But my brother and I split up ways then, because when I went with Milt Senior, he stayed on with the Speed Webb band, so by the time I got to Chicago, I was in Toledo, I was on my own, away from Gus. Since we left school together, we had been together until that period in Toledo.

But in Chicago, it was still a spit away from the Milt Senior band to play with Eddie Mallory, an excellent lead trumpet player.
And we had a good band, too.
What was that guitar player's name? I see it all the time, and now he's a dear friend of mine.
Yeah. And also at Buchet's was the first nightclub appearance of the famous fan dancer, Sally Rand -- we played her first nightclub act.
Uh huh. And she later became very famous at the World's Fair there.
Tell us about that. That was in Chicago -- the Villa DeNice.

Yes, it was like fairyland out there in the suburbs of Chicago. They had an artiifical lake and a lagoon, and little streams flowing in the back with gondoliers singing, just like in Venice, Italy. And the show was all European acts -- like adaggio dancers and South American acts and European type acts. The singers were all clasically oriented; they would do -- I remember one wonderful tenor, an Italian tenor, he would do bits from 'La Tasca', the opera, you know, little arias andthen he would do certain popular songs that were suitable for a classical voice -- I'll never forget how he used to sing 'Softly as the Morning Sunrise', the best I ever heard it sung.
The jazz musicians have just since discovered that song and improvised on it. But oh, the way he sang that piece was something. But those were the particular kinds of

And you guys, you musicians -- you were academic musicians, black musicians, that could comply -- this was one of the few places where outside of the theatre, where a black musican was qualified to play, because true, he was qualified to play any kind of music.

Right, we were like studio musicians. We played good dance music, we played jazz numbers with jazz improvisation in them, and we read this music of these European acts, when we were playing pretty classical music.

I remember one act did -- performed a very famous classical thing, 'In A Persian Market,' or something like that -- I think it was by somebody like Rimsky-Korsakov or something, but you got to play it well for these European acts. So we had to do that, along with our own music and the popular dance music of the day, and you know -- in those days, we just discovered, we were so crazy about the new writers, Rogers and Hart, and we played 'Dancing on the Ceiling.' and 'You Took Advantage Of Me.'
Oh yeah; that was a beautiful song.
And they wrote some lovely songs.
